subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw accept this exact-head native MXC SDK/node-pty dependency graph and the SDK's argv-carried base64 config envelope for a first-party external sandbox plugin?
rationale: The code defect is mechanically fixable, but accepting packaged native executables, install-script dependency behavior, and the preview MXC config transport is a maintainer/secops boundary choice that automation cannot approve.

options.title: Fix Then Approve Exact Head
options.body: Require the registration-mode fix and focused test first, then approve `/allow-dependencies-change` for the final SHA if secops accepts the MXC preview boundary.

options.title: Pause For Upstream Transport
options.body: Hold the PR until MXC provides a non-argv config transport or OpenClaw adds a narrower wrapper contract for sensitive sandbox payloads.

options.title: Decline First-Party Packaging
options.body: Close or redirect the backend to an external ClawHub-only experiment if maintainers do not want to own this native sandbox/security surface in the OpenClaw repo.

recommendation.title: Fix Then Approve Exact Head
recommendation.body: Require the registration-mode fix and focused test first, then approve `/allow-dependencies-change` for the final SHA if secops accepts the MXC preview boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They posted the latest parity request and have the most recent review context for the remaining code and acceptance questions.
